test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A single discount equivalent to successive discounts of 40% and 20% is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Successive Discount** = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, a = 40 and b = 20.

Effective Discount = 40 + 20 − (40 × 20) ÷ 100

Effective Discount = 60 − 800 ÷ 100 = 60 − 8 = 52%.

**∴ The correct answer is 52%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 40%, Second discount = 20%.
**Formulas:** SP = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% | Equivalent Discount = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79759d937c9647ade00c125da2c6bc92dc5899040ac229e86404e80fab0744aa.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.

⇒ Price after 40% discount = 100 − 40 = 60.

⇒ Price after 20% additional discount = 60 − (20% of 60) = 60 − 12 = 48.

⇒ Total Discount = MP − Final SP = 100 − 48 = 52.

⇒ **Equivalent Discount Percentage** = (52 ÷ 100) × 100 = 52%.

**∴ The correct answer is 52%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the reduced price, they are called **successive discounts**. The net discount is always less than the sum of individual discount rates.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price − Discount.</p
